scenarios.title: The Younger Generation
scenarios.text: A rookie asks how you handle the pressure, standing by the kicking net after practice, and you realize you've never once said it out loud.

choices.label: Say it out loud
choices.result: For the first time, you find the words: the breath, the one thought, the forgetting. He writes them down, and so, later, do you.

choices.label: Show him instead
choices.result: Not words: you take him to the field and show him your routine, breath by breath, kick by kick. He gets it faster that way.

choices.label: Tell him it comes with time
choices.result: It comes with time, you tell him. It's true, and it isn't much help, and you think about it on the drive home.

scenarios.title: The New Home
scenarios.text: Your family has outgrown the house: three kids, two dogs, one bathroom that everybody fights over every morning, and a garage completely full of kicking nets.

choices.label: Let the kids choose their rooms
choices.result: A bigger house, and the kids pick their rooms first, loudly. The move is chaotic and happy, and the dogs love the yard.

choices.label: Add a room instead
choices.result: An addition instead of a move, built over the offseason. The kids keep their school and their friends, and you keep your street.

choices.label: Make it work another year
choices.result: One more year in the small house, creatively. It's crowded and warm, you build bunk beds yourself, badly, and {sibling} helps.

scenarios.title: The Injury Prevention Debate
scenarios.text: You and a trainer disagree about your recovery routine: they want more rest days; you want more work. It's turned into an argument in front of the whole training room.

choices.label: Compare the numbers
choices.result: Both of you bring numbers to a meeting. The routine you end up with is better than either plan, and you shake hands.

choices.label: Do it your way
choices.result: Your way, with more work. Your leg holds, and the trainer stays unconvinced and writes it down in your file.

choices.label: Trust the trainer this time
choices.result: The trainer's way, this time, without arguing at all. They notice the trust, and your body thanks you for it by November.

scenarios.title: The Veteran's Committee
scenarios.text: Teammates ask you to represent them in a hard conversation with the coaches: practices are too long, the young players are exhausted, and two have been hurt.

choices.label: Speak for them
choices.result: Their case, made calmly and clearly by you in the coaches' office. The coaches change one thing, the practice length, and the room notices who asked.

choices.label: Bring a proposal
choices.result: A proposal, not a complaint: a new practice schedule with the same work in less time. The coaches adopt half of it.

choices.label: Suggest a captain
choices.result: A captain should do it, you suggest. One does, less well, and the young players stop asking you for things.

scenarios.title: The Charity Board
scenarios.text: A children's nonprofit you've supported for years invites you to join its board. The meetings are monthly, the budget is tight, and the work is real.

choices.label: Join and work
choices.result: You join and actually work: budgets, hiring, a summer program. The meetings run long, and you've never been prouder of a spreadsheet.

choices.label: Join as an adviser
choices.result: You join as an adviser, with a seat at four meetings a year. You help where a famous name helps and stay out of the rest.

choices.label: Stay a donor
choices.result: A polite no to the board, and a generous donation with a long letter. They read the letter aloud at their next meeting.

scenarios.title: The Business Partner's Exit
scenarios.text: A partner wants out of a business you built together: the restaurant, the dealership, the start-up, whichever it is. He's tired, and he wants his money back by spring.

choices.label: Buy him out fairly
choices.result: A fair buyout, with lawyers and a handshake at the end. He leaves happy, and the business is all yours now, for better and worse.

choices.label: Sell it together
choices.result: You both sell, and split it evenly down the middle. The business goes to new owners, and the friendship stays completely intact.

choices.label: Run it alone
choices.result: Alone, with his share bought on a payment plan. It's more work than you thought, and you learn a great deal about payroll.

scenarios.title: Everyone Wants You There
scenarios.text: Your family wants you at more events than you can make: a cousin's wedding, a niece's recital, {parent}'s retirement party, a reunion. All of them are in October.

choices.label: Pick the ones that matter most
choices.result: The ones that matter most, chosen carefully: {parent}'s party and the recital. You make every one, and nobody asks about the rest.

choices.label: Share your calendar
choices.result: Your whole calendar, shared with the family. The arguments get shorter, and the cousin moves the wedding by a week.

choices.label: Promise the offseason
choices.result: The offseason, promised to everyone, and kept. It's a long wait, and the family photos from October are missing you.

scenarios.title: The New Contract Structure
scenarios.text: The club offers a shorter deal with incentives you're not sure you'll hit: percentages, long kicks, playoff games. Your agent calls it 'a bet on you'.

choices.label: Sign and chase them
choices.result: Signed, and every incentive goes on the inside of your locker. You chase them all season, and you hit two of three.

choices.label: Negotiate the incentives down
choices.result: The incentives, renegotiated to numbers you can actually hit. It takes a week, and the club agrees because you asked nicely.

choices.label: Ask {holder} what they think
choices.result: {holder}, who has watched every one of your kicks, says 'Sign it' without hesitation. You do, and you feel calm about it all season.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Rumors
scenarios.text: The media have started asking how much longer you'll play: at your locker, on the radio, in a column titled 'The Last Good Years'. You're thirty-one, and you feel fine.

choices.label: Give the same answer every time
choices.result: 'As long as I'm good,' every time, to every reporter, word for word. They stop asking by October, bored, which was the point.

choices.label: Joke about the question
choices.result: A joke about needing a walker for the post-game interview. The clip goes around the league, and the columnist writes a nicer column.

choices.label: Stop answering questions
choices.result: Practice instead of interviews, every single day. Your silence says more than any answer could, and your kicks say all the rest.

scenarios.title: The Rookie's Confidence
scenarios.text: A young teammate is crumbling under online criticism after a bad game: he's stopped eating lunch with the team, and he reads the comments in the training room between treatments.

choices.label: Tell him about your worst week
choices.result: Your worst week as a pro, told to him in full, in an empty meeting room. He laughs at the worst part, which is how you know it worked.

choices.label: Take him to dinner
choices.result: Dinner, with no football talk at all: his hometown, his family, his terrible taste in music. He comes back to lunch the next day.

choices.label: Get him off the apps
choices.result: Delete them, you tell him, for one month. He does it, grudgingly, and by the end of the month he's himself again.

scenarios.title: The Former Coach's Advice
scenarios.text: An old coach, retired now, calls on a Sunday and tells you to start thinking about your next chapter. 'Not because you're done,' he says. 'Because you'll be surprised how fast it comes.'

choices.label: Make a list
choices.result: A list of things you'd want to do after football, started that night on the back of a playbook. It's longer than you expected, and some of it excites you.

choices.label: Ask him what he did
choices.result: What did he do when it ended? He tells you, over an hour, the hard parts included, and you take notes without meaning to.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: Not yet, you tell him, there's more kicking in you. He laughs and says that's what he said, and hangs up kindly.

scenarios.title: A Town's Thank-You
scenarios.text: Your hometown wants to honor your career with a dinner, a plaque and a key to the city, and you're still playing it. The mayor's office has already printed the invitations.

choices.label: Accept with your family beside you
choices.result: Accepted, with {parent} and {sibling} at the head table. It's a great night, and {parent} keeps the key to the city in his truck.

choices.label: Ask them to wait until you're done
choices.result: Wait until you're done, you ask kindly. They agree, a little relieved, and it gives you something to look forward to.

choices.label: Turn it into a youth clinic
choices.result: A youth clinic instead of a dinner: two hundred kids, a muddy field, and the mayor holding for you once, badly.

scenarios.title: The Guest Analyst
scenarios.text: A network offers you a guest analyst spot during your off week: a studio, a tie, a monitor full of other kickers, and a producer in your ear.

choices.label: Do it and enjoy it
choices.result: You do it, and you're good at it, explaining a kick in ways nobody has heard before. Your phone fills with texts from teammates and agents.

choices.label: Prepare like a game week
choices.result: Film of every kicker in the league, studied for three days. You say one smart thing on air, and it's the clip of the week.

choices.label: Rest during the off week
choices.result: No studio this time. It's your off week, and your body and your family come first, so the network books a punter instead.
